family_naming_note: The catalog calls this family 'H. 36' inside the wall chapter, and calls a DIFFERENT family 'H. 36' nowhere else - but H.48, H.60, H.84 and H.96 name both a base family and a wall family. The registry merges section files by family NAME, so wall families are namespaced 'Wall H.xx' to keep two unrelated families from merging into one. The catalog's own wording is preserved in 'section'.
extraction_note: printed p.211, now WHOLE - all three opening kinds. The push-up type was held back on 2026-08-18 for want of a drawing convention; on 2026-08-20 that was judged the wrong shape of blocker. The codes are catalog FACT and the missing symbol is a drawing question, so the data ships and front_layout carries a mechanism with NO hinge_axis - 70_symbols draws a leaf only when told an axis, so nothing is drawn rather than something wrong. Same treatment as base_pull_out_door on printed p.36. printed p.212 (compound units) is still deferred - internal partitions are new geometry. | 2026-10-04, group 1 of the catalog recon: printed p.212 taken WHOLE - the three compound positions, 13 codes, twins of H.48 printed p.215-216. The 2026-08-18 blocker (internal partitions are new geometry) was retired by the H.48 extraction, which records the partition as modules_mm and draws one front - the same treatment here.

data.mounting_note: Catalog-level fact: every unit in the wall chapter hangs. HOW HIGH it hangs is not in the catalog and is not here - the generator takes it from Standards::WALL_MOUNT_BOTTOM_MM, a project default awaiting M1.6, and writes it onto the object as mount_bottom_mm (Contract v1.5).
data.n_elle_note: Each wall page carries a second elevation labelled 'N- Elle' at H + 2,2 (38,2 here). N_Elle is its own chapter, printed p.321. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED: the +22 mm belongs to that front programme and must not be baked into this family's height. CORRECTION 2026-08-23, evening (learned rule 9 - added, not erased): THIS FIGURE IS NOT PRINTED ON THE PAGE. pdftotext -bbox puts 'N- Elle' at a normal 7,5 pt over the perspective drawing on every wall page of this chapter; rendering exactly that box at 400 and at 600 dpi shows blank paper. It is white text, or a hidden layer for the N_Elle edition - IN THE FILE, NOT IN THE BOOK. The wording above ('the elevation carries', 'the second elevation on this page') is therefore wrong, and the H.48 note's guess that the 170-dpi render merely lacked resolution is wrong too. THE NUMBER STAYS, RELABELLED: a document lead BELOW source trust, used for nothing and not to be quoted to Elda as something the catalog prints. Learned rule 10 says the render is the page; this is the first time the text layer claimed something the page does not, and it will not be the last.

wall_push_up_door.description: Wall unit with push-up door - 1 push-up door - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_push_up_door.notes: Narrower width set than the other two types on this page: W.60-120, with no W.45. Extracted as DATA with no opening symbol, decided 2026-08-20 - see extraction_note. The page lists Valencia handle 23, Servo Drive mechanism 554 and Power adapter 224 as surcharges with no article code; not recorded as companion_refs (Elda Q8).

front_layout.note: One full-front leaf carried by a push-up mechanism. Deliberately NO hinge_axis: the travel is not a swing about an edge, so the Drawing_Spec hinge rule cannot describe it and no elevation V is ever drawn. What IS drawn is open_leaf below - the front itself, dashed, where it ends up.

open_leaf.frame: y from the FRONT FACE (negative = in front of it), z from the CARCASS BASE. Both mm. The two entries are the leaf's long edges; the slab is swept across the full unit width and thickened on its outer face.
open_leaf.source_ref: printed p.560 / PDF 562, 'Vertical push-up door system h. 36'
open_leaf.note: VERTICAL system: the leaf does not rotate at all, it rides up on parallel arms and stays vertical. Printed 33,5 / 15 / 21 / 36 - top edge 335 above the carcass top, 150 in front of the face, so the bottom edge sits 25 BELOW the top. The swept maximum during travel is 210, wider than the final 150; recorded here, not drawn.
